text:
Maya: Heads-up — noticed quota attribution drops for a subset of requests when they hit the project-fallback routing. Console shows requests counted under 'unknown' project sometimes. Anyone seen this?
Kris: Hmm, do you have an example request id?
Maya: yup: req=0f3b2a. Happened ~ 10:23 PST. I can paste headers.
Sam: That sounds like the authn->authz handoff failing to populate project claim before quota evaluation. We saw a similar blip last month but it was transient.
Maya: here's the headers we capture (sanitized):
```
x-origin: service-A
authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]
x-project-id: missing
x-auth-exchange: proxy-v2
```
Jules: If x-project-id is missing, the router should fallback to origin affinity then to project mapping table. Did the origin lookup fail?
Maya: router matched origin -> project mapping fine for most requests, but these had a short-circuit to project-fallback path (we route to tenant-default when claims absent). Those tenants show zero attribution.
Kris: Could be a race where exchange-service hasn't returned the claim before quota check. We added a 20ms cache TTL recently.
Ada: Is that the new delegation-exchange canary? We rolled a flag last night to speed up exchange (reduce syncs) — might be related.
Sam: @Ada can you confirm which flag? If it's the canary that switches to async exchange, quota checks might run before authz finishes.
Ada: confirmed: flag=async-exchange-quickpath. Enabled for 12% of traffic on prod around 02:00 UTC.
Maya: timeline matches. The strange part is requests are still served successfully, just mis-attributed for billing/telemetry.
Kris: Right, serving isn't blocked because the fallback path is permissive, but attribution is lost. That explains errors in the dashboard totals.
Jules: For remediation we can either 1) pause the flag, 2) make quota evaluation wait for exchange up to a short threshold, or 3) add best-effort attribution post-hoc in the telemetry pipeline. Tradeoffs: 1 is fastest, 2 increases tail latency, 3 is eventually consistent and harder to reconcile for real-time quotas.
Sam: I'd prefer #3 as short-term: emit a post-attribution event with request id and claims, then adjust billing/telemetry. But quota enforcement needs immediate accuracy.
Kris: We should avoid increasing request latency for all traffic. Can we gate waiting on exchange only when router sees no project claim and request looks billable?
Ada: technically yes — we already have a path decision in the router. We can make it conditional: blocking wait only if is_billable and not from internal-proxy.
Maya: OK. For now can we throttle the canary to 5% while we patch post-attribution?
Ada: done — scaled back flag to 5% at 03:12 UTC.
deploy-bot: deploy "auth-exchange-fallback-patch" to prod completed at 03:30 UTC by @Ada :thumbsup:
Kris: I'll open a tiny PR to add a post-attribution event (kafka topic: auth.post_attrib) and a reconciliation job that fixes daily totals.
Jules: Also add a dashboard card showing 'attribution-lag' metric (percent of requests reconciled after X hours) so we can see regressions.
Sam: Good idea. Add an alert if attribution-lag > 2% for > 1h.
Maya: can someone own the rollout notes? Need to communicate to billing and CS that some invoices may be adjusted for yesterday.
Kris: I'll draft a short blurb and ping billing.
Ada: I'll follow up with detailed flag timeline and cluster ids.
Maya: thanks all. If anything else pops up, tag me.
Kris: quick note for the action items: 1) PR for auth.post_attrib (Kris) 2) reconciliation job (Kris/Sam) 3) dashboard card + alert (Jules) 4) rollout notes (Kris) 5) flag telemetry log (Ada).
Maya: perfect.
Sam: re: implementation detail for post-attrib — we should include request latency, route, model, and original headers so the billing job can do accurate mapping.
Kris: agreed. I'll include a small schema in the PR.
Maya: closing loop — will confirm once billing confirms receipt. :white_check_mark:
